position_in_era.historical_role: The most direct Britpop heir to the arena-rock dual-protagonist structure: Liam Gallagher's detached, nasal vocal delivers the verses, then the song opens into a sustained guitar outro where Noel Gallagher and guest Paul Weller extend the solo across what became 5+ additional minutes in live performance. The Noel/Liam sibling tension — two voices with the same blood but different aesthetics — mirrors the Axl/Slash dialectic of composer-vocalist versus virtuoso guitarist.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded at Rockfield Studios, Wales, and RAK Studios, London (1994–1995). Producer: Owen Morris. Duration: 7:27 (album version). Paul Weller appears as guest on lead guitar, backing vocals, and whistle. Owen Morris added a Mellotron to the arrangement. The song serves as the closing track on Morning Glory, giving it the structural position of a coda or valediction.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Liam Gallagher (vocal) as the aria protagonist — expressionless, delivered as though reciting received wisdom. Noel Gallagher (guitar) as the solo protagonist — the closing guitar section is Noel's compositional signature. Paul Weller's guest guitar adds a third voice. In live performance, the song's outro becomes a platform for extended Noel improvisation.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Liam: lead vocals. Noel: lead and acoustic guitars. Paul Weller: lead guitar, whistle. Paul 'Bonehead' Arthurs: rhythm guitar. Paul McGuigan: bass. Alan White: drums. Owen Morris: Mellotron overdub.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: (What's the Story) Morning Glory? was the second-best-selling album in UK chart history at time of release. 'Champagne Supernova' as the album closer positioned it as the definitive statement of Britpop's relationship to rock epic forms — a form inherited from Bohemian Rhapsody through GnR.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Album October 1995. Never released as a UK single (only US/Australia). Duration and position on the album designated it as an album-track statement rather than a radio hit — the dual-protagonist structure was allowed to breathe at full length.
